stories.stat_label: of bamboo cribs off the coast
stories.headline: Bamboo and oyster shells stopped a village's floods
stories.summary: In Pamarawan, the Philippines' first nature-based sea defence uses bamboo cribs plus oyster shells in coconut-husk nets to break waves. The village no longer floods.
stories.why: The cribs trap mud so mangroves can be planted, making the shore stronger every year.

stories.headline: The universe's oldest light reveals spinning cosmic gas
stories.summary: Columbia astronomers averaged Big Bang afterglow data around 25 galaxy clusters and found a faint hot-cold pattern: evidence that gas inside the clusters is rotating.
stories.why: It's a new way to watch giant clusters move, using light from 380,000 years after the Big Bang.

stories.stat_label: lower dementia risk with bright days
stories.headline: More bright daylight was linked to 16% less dementia
stories.summary: Wrist sensors tracked light for 87,577 adults over about 8 years. Those in brighter daytime light had a 16% lower dementia risk; under 42 minutes a day was a strong warning sign.
stories.why: It's a link, not proof, but a walk outside is an easy habit to try.

stories.headline: Fishers on Pemba asked for new marine parks, and got 2
stories.summary: After catches kept shrinking, more than 20 communities on Pemba's east coast worked with Tanzania's government and NGOs to create 2 marine protected areas they help manage.
stories.why: A park on Pemba's other side, made in 2005, boosted fish and fishers' incomes.

fun_fact: The Pamarawan project cost about $2 million and was inspired by mangrove work in Indonesia.
